title: Prefabricated Housing Complex
program: University of Rome Tor Vergata — Digital Processes for Building Design and Construction
description: A parametric Revit model of a 1960s prefabricated housing complex, rebuilt from historical documentation, original patents and an as-built survey.
body: A full BIM model in Revit of an existing prefabricated housing complex built in the 1960s near Milan, reconstructed from historical documentation, original construction patents and as-built conditions surveyed via Google Maps.

The model covers both architectural and structural modeling with custom parametric families — including a catalogue of façade panel types — supported by a Common Data Environment and data extraction into Excel for further analysis.

sections.title: Documentation
body: The model has no drawings to start from. Input came from three sources instead: historical construction photography of the complex going up in the 1960s, the original prefabrication patents, and an as-built survey of current conditions carried out over Google Maps.

sections.title: Model Structure
body: The reconstructed model opened up: floor slabs, the prefabricated façade panels hung off them, and the balconies — each element a family instance rather than modelled geometry.

sections.title: Parametric Families
body: Every façade panel is a parametric family carrying its own dimensions, layer build-up and position. Catalogued across the elevation, the whole envelope resolves into a set of repeating types, and each type extracts to Excel as a schedule.

scenes.title: Panel Catalogue
scenes.caption: Every façade panel typed and colour-coded across the elevation — the repeating set the whole envelope is built from.

scenes.title: Panel Data Sheet
scenes.caption: One panel type resolved in full: components, layer build-up, dimensions and its position on the south elevation.

scenes.title: Schedule Extraction
scenes.caption: The family parameters extracted as scheduled data, ready to leave the model for Excel.

sections.title: Structural Modeling
body: The structural model behind the envelope — panel-to-slab connections and the reinforcement detailing at the joints, drawn from the original patents.

sections.title: Architectural Modeling
body: The opening types that populate the panels: balcony doors, splayed windows, top-hung casements and the entrance door, each modelled as its own family.
